To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SCC of the lung is a disease that is associated with a T helper cell predominance and that the reactivity pattern of tumor cells with MAbs used in our study is not specific.
SCCs of the lung have the immunophenotype of a large cell carcinoma and that the tumor cells are positive for Leu M1 and CD16, and negative for HLA-DR.

the characterization of the lymphocyte population in pleural effusions of SCC of the lung and the immunophenotypic analysis of tumor cells from SCC in pleural effusion.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tumor cells from SCCs of the lung are not immunophenotypically different from the tumor cells of other types of carcinoma.

the immunophenotype of the lymphocytes from malignant pleural effusion is not different from that of lymphocytes from nonmalignant effusions and that the immunophenoype of the tumor cells from malignant pleural SCC is not specific for this type of carcinoma.
the immunocytochemical analysis of lymphocytes in the malignant pleural effusion is not useful, whereas the analysis of tumor cells is useful for the diagnosis of SCC of the lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the tumor cells from malignant effusions due to SCC of the lung can be recognized by immunocytochemical staining with a panel of monoclonals, but that the immunoreactivity pattern of these cells is not specific for the diagnosis of SCC.

the immunostaining with MAbs is useful for the identification of tumor cells in malignant pleural effusion, but it does not provide information on the biological behavior of the tumor cells or the lymphocyte subpopulation.
immunocytochemical analysis of pleural effusions is helpful in the differential diagnosis of pleural malignancies and in the identification of tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunocytochemical study of malignant pleural effusion is a useful method for the identification of the tumor cell type.

the lymphocyte subpopulation pattern of the malignant pleural effusion is similar in different types of malignant and nonmolecular diseases, whereas the reactivity pattern of SCC of the lung is not specific for the tumor cells.
the immunocytochemical analysis of pleural effusions is a valuable tool to identify and study the tumor cells.
